overviewHtml:
Christmas & New Year Tour in Nepal 2026/2027 Introduction

Celebrate Christmas and New Year in Nepal with an unforgettable 12-day holiday combining Himalayan scenery, UNESCO World Heritage Sites, cultural experiences, wildlife adventures and festive celebrations. This Christmas and New Year Tour in Nepal takes you from the historic streets of Kathmandu to the panoramic mountain views of Nagarkot and Pokhara, the wildlife-rich landscapes of Chitwan National Park, and the charming hill town of Bandipur.

Designed for couples, families, friends and private groups, this Nepal Christmas and New Year holiday offers a relaxed way to experience the country's culture, nature and Himalayan landscapes during the festive season. Enjoy Christmas celebrations, beautiful mountain sunrises, jungle activities, traditional villages and special New Year experiences while traveling with a local Nepal trekking and tour operator.

Our Christmas & New Year Holiday Package in Nepal can also be customized according to your preferred travel dates, hotel category, activities and budget.

Overview

Celebrate Christmas and New Year in a truly magical way with our specially crafted Christmas & New Year Holidays Package in Nepal. Nepal Unique Treks welcomes you to experience the festive season surrounded by the Himalayas, rich cultural traditions, peaceful temples, and warm Nepali hospitality. Whether you are seeking adventure, spiritual refreshment, or a relaxing holiday, Nepal offers an unforgettable winter escape.

December and January are among the best times to explore Nepal’s natural beauty. The skies remain clear, offering spectacular views of snow-capped peaks such as Annapurna, Langtang, and Everest. Our holiday package includes a blend of sightseeing, soft adventure, cultural activities, and festive celebrations designed for couples, families, and solo travelers. From exploring UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Kathmandu to enjoying serene moments by Pokhara’s Fewa Lake, every day brings a new experience.

Christmas in Nepal is celebrated with lights, music, and joyful gatherings, while New Year’s Eve brings exciting parties, traditional dinners, and breathtaking fireworks in major cities. With our well-organized itinerary, you can enjoy these celebrations without any hassle. We arrange comfortable hotels, private transfers, expert local guides, and personalized services to make your festive journey stress-free and memorable.

You can choose from a variety of activities, such as short hikes, sunrise views from Nagarkot or Sarangkot, cultural dinners, wildlife safaris in Chitwan, or thrilling adventure sports in Pokhara. Whether you prefer a peaceful celebration or an action-packed holiday, Nepal has something for everyone.

By booking your Christmas & New Year tour in Nepal with Nepal Unique Treks, you ensure a heartwarming, safe, and enriching travel experience. Come and welcome the New Year in the land of mountains, spirituality, and timeless traditions an unforgettable celebration that stays with you for life.

Trip Highlights

  • 12-day Christmas and New Year holiday in Nepal
  • Kathmandu UNESCO World Heritage Sites
  • Christmas celebration in Nepal
  • Poon Hill sunrise at 3,210 meters
  • Pokhara and Phewa Lake
  • Lumbini, the birthplace of Buddha
  • Chitwan National Park jungle activities
  • Himalayan views and winter scenery
  • Private and customizable travel options
  • Ideal for couples, families, friends and small groups

Kathmandu Valley Sightseeing

Kathmandu Valley offers a fascinating blend of ancient history, vibrant culture, and sacred heritage. During sightseeing, travelers explore UNESCO World Heritage Sites such as Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), and the historic Kathmandu Durbar Square.

These iconic landmarks showcase Nepal’s rich art, architecture, and spiritual traditions. Visitors can experience bustling local markets, traditional crafts, and centuries-old courtyards reflecting the valley’s royal past. The cultural diversity, friendly locals, and lively ambiance make Kathmandu a memorable highlight for every traveler. Perfect for photography, cultural learning, and peaceful spiritual moments, Kathmandu Valley is a must-visit destination in Nepal.

Trekking in Poon Hill

The Poon Hill Trek is a short yet rewarding trekking adventure in the Annapurna region, famous for its panoramic Himalayan sunrise. This trek takes you through charming villages, terraced fields, rhododendron forests, and warm Gurung and Magar communities. The highlight is the early-morning climb to Poon Hill (3,210m), offering 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, Machhapuchhre, and Nilgiri. Suitable for beginners, families, and short-holiday visitors, the trek combines natural beauty with cultural experiences. Comfortable teahouses, scenic trails, and breathtaking mountain vistas make Poon Hill one of Nepal’s most popular and enjoyable trekking routes.

Pokhara Valley Sightseeing

Pokhara Valley is Nepal’s ultimate destination for natural beauty, adventure, and relaxation. Surrounded by peaceful lakes and Himalayan peaks, it offers stunning views of Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range. Sightseeing includes the tranquil Fewa Lake, World Peace Pagoda, Gupteswar Mahadev Cave, Davis Falls, Bindabasini Temple, and the informative International Mountain Museum. Visitors can enjoy boating, paragliding, short hikes, and lakeside dining in a calm and refreshing environment. Pokhara is perfect for those seeking nature, culture, and gentle adventure, making it a favorite stop in every Nepal holiday package.

Lumbini – Buddha’s Birthplace

Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha, is one of the world’s most sacred pilgrimage destinations. Located in the Terai plains of Nepal, it features the Maya Devi Temple, the exact spot where Buddha was born, along with ancient ruins, monasteries, and peaceful meditation zones. The Sacred Garden, Ashoka Pillar, and international monasteries built by different countries offer deep spiritual and architectural significance. Lumbini is perfect for travelers seeking tranquility, history, and cultural understanding. A visit to this UNESCO World Heritage Site provides a profound insight into Buddhism and its global influence.

Chitwan National Park Activities

Chitwan National Park offers thrilling wildlife and jungle adventures in Nepal’s subtropical lowlands. Travelers can enjoy exciting activities such as jeep safaris, canoe rides, bird watching, jungle walks, and visits to the Elephant Breeding Center. The park is home to endangered species like the one-horned rhinoceros, Bengal tiger, gharial crocodile, and over 500 bird species. Cultural programs featuring Tharu dance and village tours add a unique local experience. Chitwan is ideal for nature lovers, wildlife enthusiasts, and families looking for safe, guided adventure in Nepal’s lush, diverse jungles.

Why Celebrate Christmas and New Year in Nepal?

Nepal offers a rare mix of crisp, clear winter skies, ancient culture, wildlife, and festive energy, without the crowds and prices of typical Western holiday destinations. December and January fall in the dry season, so you get stable weather, sharp mountain views, and a very different holiday from the usual one.

Himalayan Mountain Views

Winter is among the clearest times of year for mountain visibility. With little monsoon haze, peaks like Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Langtang stand out against deep blue skies. You can see them from Pokhara's lakeside, from hilltop viewpoints near Kathmandu, or on a scenic mountain flight toward Everest.

Christmas Celebrations in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Nagarkot

  • Kathmandu: Thamel and Durbar Marg have decorated hotels, restaurants, and cafés, along with carol services, special dinners, and live music. Churches hold Christmas Eve and Christmas Day services, and Christmas is an official public holiday in Nepal.

  • Pokhara: The Lakeside strip has a relaxed festive mood, with lakefront dinners, bonfires, and Himalayan reflections on Phewa Lake.
  • Nagarkot: This hill station is the quieter option. Many resorts offer Christmas dinners, fireplaces, and sunrise views of the Himalayas, which makes it good for a peaceful, romantic holiday.

Winter Weather

Days are generally sunny and mild, while nights and mornings get cold, especially at altitude.

  • Kathmandu: pleasant days, chilly nights
  • Pokhara: mild and comfortable, with cool mornings
  • Nagarkot and hills: cold nights, spectacular mornings
  • Chitwan (lowlands): warm days, cool, often foggy mornings

Pack layers, since the temperature swing between day and night can be large.

UNESCO Heritage Sites

Nepal has several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and winter's dry weather makes sightseeing easy. The Kathmandu Valley alone has seven protected monument zones, including:

  • Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur Durbar Squares
  • Swayambhunath (the "Monkey Temple")
  • Boudhanath Stupa
  • Pashupatinath Temple
  • Changu Narayan Temple

Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, is also a major draw, and Chitwan and Sagarmatha (Everest) are listed as natural sites.

Chitwan Jungle Safari

Winter is a good season for wildlife in Chitwan National Park. The grass is shorter, which makes animals easier to spot. Typical experiences include jeep safaris, canoe rides, and guided jungle walks. You can look for one-horned rhinoceroses, deer, crocodiles, and a wide variety of birds, and with luck, a Bengal tiger. Tharu cultural dances in the evening round it off. Chitwan pairs well with a Christmas or New Year itinerary because it is warm when the hills are cold.

Nepalese Culture

The holiday season is a good time to experience Nepal's living traditions. Around the end of December you may catch local festivals such as Yomari Punhi (a Newar festival with sweet steamed dumplings) and Tamu Lhosar (the Gurung New Year, usually around December 30). Visits to temples, monasteries, and local homes, plus cooking classes for dishes like momos and dal bhat, give you a cultural side to the trip that most holiday destinations can't match.

New Year's Eve Celebrations

Nepal's traditional new year follows the Bikram Sambat calendar and falls in mid-April, but the international New Year is widely celebrated, especially in tourist areas.

  • Kathmandu (Thamel): parties, DJ nights, hotel galas, and rooftop dinners
  • Pokhara: lakeside parties, bonfires, and live music
  • Nagarkot and resorts: quiet fireside countdowns and sunrise views on New Year's Day

You can choose anything from a lively party to a calm countdown under the stars.

Private and Customizable Tours

Nepal suits tailor-made travel. Private tours can be built around your interests, pace, and budget, with your own guide and driver. Typical combinations include culture plus nature (Kathmandu, Pokhara, Chitwan), short scenic hikes, a Himalayan flight, spa and wellness stays, and extensions to Bhutan or Tibet. Private itineraries also let you time the Christmas and New Year dates exactly as you like.

Family-Friendly Travel

Nepal can work very well for families. Kids enjoy elephant-free wildlife safaris (look for ethical operators), boat rides on Phewa Lake, easy village walks, kite-flying, and hands-on activities like pottery in Bhaktapur. Winter's dry, mild days make sightseeing comfortable, and many hotels offer family rooms and festive meals. Choose lower-altitude destinations and shorter drives for younger children.

Couple and Honeymoon Options

Nepal is a strong romantic choice thanks to its scenery and privacy.

  • Sunrise and sunset over the Himalayas from Nagarkot or Pokhara
  • Boutique resorts and lodges with fireplaces and mountain-view rooms
  • Candlelit lakeside dinners in Pokhara
  • Private jungle lodges in Chitwan
  • Couples' spa treatments and sunrise yoga
  • Scenic helicopter or mountain flights

itinerary.title: Welcome to Nepal in Kathmandu International Airport 1345 m
itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (6.5 km from the city center), our representative will greet you and transfer you to your hotel in Kathmandu. After check-in, you will receive a short briefing about the trip, permits, and necessary preparations. Depending on your arrival time, you may explore nearby markets, local temples, or simply rest after your long flight. In the evening, enjoy a welcome Nepali dinner and relax at your hotel. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu valley exploring with private tour guide (Sightseeing) 1345m, 5 hrs
itinerary.description: Today, you explore the cultural treasures of Kathmandu Valley with a private tour guide. Visit UNESCO World Heritage Sites such as Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, and Kathmandu Durbar Square. Your guide will explain the religious and historical significance of each monument. Driving distances are short—typically 2–5 km between major landmarks. Enjoy views of vibrant streets, sacred temples, and centuries-old architecture. Return to the hotel in the evening for preparation for the next day’s journey. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: m, Flight to Pokhara International Airport and drive to Ulleri Village 2050m, 3 hrs
itinerary.description: Take a scenic 30-minute flight to Pokhara International Airport (820 m), where the Annapurna Himalaya greets you with stunning views. After landing, drive about 42 km toward Nayapul and further uphill to Ulleri Village. The road gradually climbs through terraced farmland, traditional Magar settlements, and forested hills. The final section ascends to Ulleri at 2050 m, famous for its stone steps and panoramic landscape. Spend the afternoon exploring the village and preparing for tomorrow’s trek. Overnight in Ulleri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani Village 2874m, 5/6 hrs
itinerary.description: Begin your beautiful trekking day with a steady climb through rhododendron and oak forests. The trail covers approximately 10–12 km, gradually gaining altitude as you ascend toward Ghorepani. Enjoy refreshing mountain air, sounds of birds, and views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli along the way. Pass through Banthanti and Nangethanti before reaching Ghorepani, a charming Gurung and Magar village at 2,874 m. Famous for its viewpoints and colorful tea houses, Ghorepani provides spectacular sunset views over the mountains. Overnight in Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Visit Poon Hill 3210m, Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani 2630m, 6 hours
itinerary.description: Early in the morning, hike 1.5 km uphill to Poon Hill (3,210 m) for a breathtaking sunrise over Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and Nilgiri. After descending back to Ghorepani, enjoy breakfast and begin your trek to Tadapani. The route covers about 8–9 km through dense rhododendron forest, ridge walks, and scenic descents. This section is rich in wildlife, including langur monkeys and various bird species. Reach Tadapani (2,630 m), known for its close-up view of Annapurna South and Fishtail. Overnight in Tadapani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Ghandruk and drive to Pokhara 4 hrs Trek, 3 hours drive, 810m
itinerary.description: Descend approximately 7 km from Tadapani to Ghandruk, a stunning Gurung village famous for culture, stone houses, and mountain views. The trek takes around 4 hours through forested paths and terraced fields. Explore Ghandruk’s traditional museum and enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. After lunch, drive 3 hours (about 55 km) back to Pokhara. Spend your evening relaxing at Lakeside or exploring the peaceful Fewa Lake area. Overnight in Pokhara (810 m).

itinerary.title: Pokhara Valley Sightseeing 810m, 5/6 hrs
itinerary.description: Enjoy a full day of sightseeing around Pokhara Valley. Visit the World Peace Pagoda for breathtaking lake and mountain views, the Gupteswar Mahadev Cave, Devi’s Waterfall, and the International Mountain Museum, which showcases Nepal’s mountaineering history. Drive about 20–25 km in total during the day. Stroll around Phewa Lake and visit Barahi Temple, situated on an island. Pokhara offers a perfect blend of natural beauty and cultural heritage. Overnight in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Lumbini 258 km, 6/7 hrs
itinerary.description: Today, drive approximately 258 km from Pokhara to Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha. The journey follows the Siddhartha Highway, passing through lush hills, charming villages, and river valleys. After arriving in Lumbini (150 m), check in to your hotel and visit the nearby sacred garden if time permits. Lumbini is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its monasteries, Maya Devi Temple, Ashoka Pillar, and spiritual ambiance. Overnight in Lumbini.

itinerary.title: Drive from Lumbini to Chitwan National Park 162km, 2 hours 30 minuts
itinerary.description: After breakfast, drive about 162 km to Chitwan National Park. The road is smooth and scenic, passing through plains and small towns. Upon arrival, check in at your jungle resort and receive a briefing about the upcoming wildlife activities. In the afternoon, enjoy a short walk or visit a Tharu cultural village. The region sits at around 150 m elevation and is known for its warm climate and rich biodiversity. Overnight in Chitwan.

itinerary.title: Chitwan National Park Activities 150m, 5/6 hours
itinerary.description: Enjoy a full day of exciting jungle activities inside Chitwan National Park, a UNESCO site famous for Bengal tigers, one-horned rhinos, crocodiles, deer, and over 500 bird species. Activities include canoeing, jungle walk, elephant breeding center visit, jeep safari, and bird watching. Total walking and safari distance varies between 10–20 km depending on the chosen program. Experience the unique Tharu cultural show in the evening. Overnight in Chitwan.

itinerary.title: Chitwan to Kathmandu by private Car, 150m, 5/6 hours
itinerary.description: Drive approximately 160–170 km back to Kathmandu by private car, following the Trishuli River corridor. Enjoy scenic views of hills, rivers, and villages along the Prithvi Highway. Once you reach Kathmandu (1,345 m), check into your hotel and enjoy free time for shopping or relaxing. In the evening, join a farewell dinner with the Nepal Unique Treks team. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure to International Airport 1345m, 6.5 km, 30 minuts
itinerary.description: After breakfast, our team will transfer you 6.5 km to Tribhuvan International Airport for your final departure. We ensure a smooth and timely drop-off for your flight. Thank you for traveling with Nepal Unique Treks!

usefulInfoHtml:
Traveller Useful Information

This tour is designed to be flexible, so it works for many kinds of travelers. The combination of easy sightseeing, mild winter days, and a choice between festive and peaceful settings means almost everyone can find a version that suits them.

Couples

Couples get the romantic side of Nepal: sunrise over the Himalayas from Nagarkot, candlelit lakeside dinners in Pokhara, cozy boutique lodges with fireplaces, and quiet countdowns to the New Year. It also suits honeymooners and anniversary trips, since the itinerary can include private moments, spa time, and scenic flights.

Families

Families will find a comfortable pace with short travel days, easy village walks, boat rides on Phewa Lake, wildlife safaris in Chitwan, and hands-on activities like pottery or cooking classes. Winter's dry, mild weather keeps sightseeing comfortable for children and grandparents alike, and the itinerary can be adjusted for younger kids or older relatives.

Friends

Groups of friends can enjoy Thamel's New Year's Eve parties, lakeside bonfires in Pokhara, jungle safaris, and optional short hikes or adventure activities. It's a fun way to celebrate together, with a good balance of lively evenings and shared experiences during the day.

Solo Travelers

Nepal is welcoming and easy to navigate for solo visitors. You can travel with a private guide for safety and local insight, or join the festive atmosphere in Kathmandu and Pokhara, where it's easy to meet other travelers. The holiday season means you won't feel alone at Christmas or New Year.

Private Groups

Extended families, corporate teams, friend circles, and special-occasion groups can have the tour built around them, with a private guide, vehicle, and custom schedule. Private groups can choose their own hotels, pace, activities, and even arrange a special Christmas dinner or New Year's celebration.

First-Time Visitors to Nepal

For a first visit, this tour is a great introduction. It covers the highlights (Kathmandu's UNESCO sites, Pokhara, Chitwan, and Himalayan views) in the best season for clear weather, with logistics handled for you. Guides help with culture, customs, and transport, so you can relax and enjoy it.

Travelers Looking for a Relaxed Winter Holiday

If you want a break rather than a challenge, this tour fits. There's no strenuous trekking required, just comfortable drives, scenic stops, and plenty of free time. Sunny days, warm meals, and peaceful hill stations make it an easy, restful way to spend the holidays.

Travelers Wanting Culture + Wildlife + Mountains

This is where the tour shines. In a single trip you can explore ancient temples and palaces, spot rhinos and birds in Chitwan's jungle, and wake up to Himalayan sunrises, without needing to choose between them. Few destinations pack this much variety into one itinerary.

Late December and early January fall in Nepal's dry winter season. Expect sunny, mostly rain-free days, cold mornings and nights, and some of the clearest mountain skies of the year. Conditions vary a lot by altitude, so each stop on the tour feels a little different.

December/January Temperatures

These are typical ranges, and actual weather varies from year to year.

PlaceDaytimeNight/Early Morning
Kathmandu (1,400 m)about 15-20°Cabout 2-5°C
Pokhara (800 m)about 18-22°Cabout 6-10°C
Nagarkot (2,100 m)about 10-15°Cabout 0-4°C
Chitwan (150 m)about 22-26°Cabout 8-12°C

The big swing between warm afternoons and cold nights is the main thing to plan for.

Kathmandu

Days are sunny and comfortable for sightseeing, especially in the afternoon sun. Mornings and evenings get properly cold, and most hotels and homes have little or no central heating, so rooms can feel chilly at night. Many hotels provide heaters or extra blankets, and it's worth asking. Air pollution and haze can be noticeable in the valley during winter, particularly in the mornings, so some travelers bring a light mask. Thamel and Durbar Marg are lively, with festive decorations, music, and special dinners around Christmas and New Year's Eve.

Pokhara

Pokhara is milder than Kathmandu and feels relaxed and open. Days are pleasant for boating on Phewa Lake, lakeside walks, and cafés. Mornings can be cool or foggy, but they often clear to excellent views of the Annapurna range, with Machapuchare (Fishtail) rising behind the lake. Evenings need a jacket, and bonfires and live music in Lakeside add to the holiday mood.

Nagarkot

Nagarkot is the coldest and quietest of the group. Days are sunny and crisp, nights are cold, and frost is possible in the early morning. The reward is a wide Himalayan panorama at sunrise, when the peaks catch the first light. Resorts here often have fireplaces, heaters, and Christmas dinners, which makes it a cozy, romantic stop. Bring warm layers for early sunrise viewing.

Chitwan

Chitwan is in the lowlands, so it is the warmest stop, with comfortable, sunny days. Mornings and evenings are cool, and fog is common early in the day, sometimes delaying safari starts or reducing visibility for a while. The cooler, drier season and shorter grass make wildlife easier to spot. Mosquitoes are far fewer than in summer, but a little repellent is still useful. Pack a light jacket for early jeep safaris and evening cultural programs.

Mountain Visibility

Winter is one of the best seasons for mountain views thanks to low humidity and little monsoon haze. Mornings are usually the clearest, as clouds and haze can build up later in the day. Good viewpoints include Pokhara, Nagarkot, Dhulikhel, and the Kathmandu Valley rim. Views are never guaranteed, since occasional fog or cloud can block the peaks, which is why a flexible schedule with more than one viewpoint helps.

Clothing

Layering is the key.

  • Base layers: thermal tops and leggings for cold mornings and nights
  • Mid layers: fleece or a light sweater
  • Outer layer: a warm jacket, ideally a down or insulated one for Kathmandu evenings and Nagarkot
  • Accessories: hat, gloves, and a scarf
  • Footwear: comfortable walking shoes with good grip, plus warm socks
  • Extras: sunglasses and sunscreen (the winter sun is strong), and light clothing for Chitwan afternoons

Warm clothing is easy and cheap to buy in Kathmandu if you forget something.

Winter Conditions

  • Rain: rare, with mostly dry conditions
  • Sun: strong and bright, even when the air is cold
  • Fog: common in the early morning in Pokhara and Chitwan
  • Heating: limited in many buildings, so cold rooms are normal
  • Roads: generally good, but fog can slow travel, and mountain roads take time
  • Daylight: sunset comes early, around 5:30 pm, so evenings are long

What Travelers Should Expect

  • A festive but not overly commercial Christmas: celebrations are concentrated in hotels, restaurants, and tourist areas, and Christmas is a quiet public holiday for many locals.
  • Lively New Year's Eve in Thamel and Pokhara, and calm options in Nagarkot and resorts.
  • Busy tourist areas, since this is a peak season. Booking hotels and flights early is wise.
  • Sunny sightseeing days and cold nights, so a good mix of warm clothing and light layers.
  • Occasional delays from fog, traffic, or road conditions, so build in some flexibility.
  • A warm welcome and good food, including hot tea, momos, and dal bhat, which suit the cold weather well.

  • Private, customizable itineraries. Your trip is built around your group, whether that's a festive family getaway, a trek, or a cultural journey.
  • Flexible travel dates. Choose the dates that fit your holiday schedule, with no fixed departures to work around.

liveFaqs.question: Is Nepal a good destination for Christmas and New Year?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. December and January fall in the dry season, with sunny days, clear Himalayan views, and comfortable sightseeing weather. You also get cultural sites, wildlife, festive dining, and New Year's Eve celebrations, usually at lower prices than typical Western holiday destinations.

liveFaqs.question: Where can I celebrate Christmas in Nepal?
liveFaqs.answer: Kathmandu (Thamel and Durbar Marg), Pokhara (Lakeside), and Nagarkot are the most popular choices. Kathmandu and Pokhara have decorated hotels, festive dinners, live music, and church services. Nagarkot offers a quieter, cozier Christmas with fireplaces and mountain views.

liveFaqs.question: Where is the best place to celebrate New Year in Nepal?
liveFaqs.answer: It depends on your style. Thamel in Kathmandu and Lakeside in Pokhara are best for parties, DJ nights, and bonfires. Nagarkot and resort stays suit travelers who prefer a calm countdown and a Himalayan sunrise on New Year's Day.

liveFaqs.question: What is the weather like in Nepal during Christmas?
liveFaqs.answer: Expect mostly dry, sunny days and cold nights. Kathmandu is about 15-20°C by day, Pokhara is slightly milder, Nagarkot is colder, and Chitwan is the warmest. Morning fog is common in Pokhara and Chitwan, and it usually clears by mid-morning.

liveFaqs.question: Is December a good time to visit Nepal?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes, it is part of the peak travel season. Low humidity and little rain give some of the clearest mountain views of the year, and the weather suits sightseeing, safaris, and scenic drives. Because it is busy, book hotels and flights early.

liveFaqs.question: Can I customize the Christmas and New Year tour?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. You can adjust the number of days, destinations, hotels, activities, and pace to match your interests and budget. Common add-ons include a mountain flight, a short hike, spa stays, cooking classes, or extensions to Bhutan or Tibet.

liveFaqs.question: Is this Christmas tour suitable for families?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. The tour uses short travel days, gentle sightseeing, boat rides, wildlife safaris, and hands-on cultural activities. Itineraries can be adjusted for young children or older relatives, and family rooms are available at many hotels.

liveFaqs.question: Can I book a private Christmas and New Year tour in Nepal?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. Private tours include your own guide and vehicle, with a schedule built around your group. They suit couples, families, friends, and special-occasion groups, and you can arrange a private Christmas dinner or New Year's celebration.

liveFaqs.question: What is included in the Christmas and New Year package?
liveFaqs.answer: Inclusions vary by package, but typically cover: Airport pickups and drop-offs Hotel accommodation with breakfast Private transport with a driver English-speaking guide Sightseeing with entrance fees Chitwan safari activities and meals at the lodge Festive Christmas or New Year's Eve dinner (where specified) Government taxes and service charges

liveFaqs.question: What is excluded from the package?
liveFaqs.answer: Typically excluded: International flights and Nepal visa fees Travel and medical insurance Lunches and dinners not mentioned in the itinerary Personal expenses, laundry, and drinks Optional activities (such as a mountain flight) Tips for guides and drivers Costs from unforeseen delays or changes

liveFaqs.question: What should I pack for Nepal in December and January?
liveFaqs.answer: Pack in layers: thermal base layers, a fleece, and a warm down or insulated jacket, plus a hat, gloves, and a scarf. Bring comfortable walking shoes, warm socks, sunglasses, and sunscreen. Add light clothing for Chitwan afternoons, a small amount of insect repellent, and a power adapter. Warm clothing is easy to buy in Kathmandu if you forget something.

liveFaqs.question: How cold is Nepal during Christmas and New Year?
liveFaqs.answer: It's mild by day and cold at night. Kathmandu usually drops to about 2-5°C at night, and Nagarkot can reach around 0-4°C, with possible frost. Daytime sun keeps things comfortable, around 15-20°C in Kathmandu. Many buildings have limited heating, so ask your hotel for heaters or extra blankets.
